forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee - Annual Treasury Management Report 2025-26
findings.headline: £350k reserve maintained against possible non-extension of statutory override on pooled investment fund accounting beyond 2029
findings.detail: The council previously set aside £350k to mitigate the impact if the statutory override on accounting for gains and losses in pooled investment funds was not extended. Although the override may continue to April 2029, the council has decided to maintain this reserve against the risk of future extension denial.
findings.matters: Policy uncertainty on investment accounting treatment creates a contingent liability; the reserve protects against potential balance sheet volatility if the override lapses in 2029.
findings.quote: The Council had set up a reserve of £350k to mitigate the impact of the statutory override not being extended. In view of the fact that the override may not be extended past 2029 the authority has decided to maintain this reserve

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee - Annual Treasury Management Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Non-treasury commercial property portfolio of £3.98m generating 6.45% return but concentrated in 11 properties
findings.detail: The council holds a longstanding portfolio of 11 commercial investment properties within the borough, valued at £3.983m. These are held for commercial return (not treasury management) and generated £257k income in 2025-26. The 6.45% return exceeds treasury yields but represents concentrated local real estate exposure.
findings.matters: This non-treasury investment concentration in local commercial property creates undiversified exposure to borough economic conditions and property market risk; material if any tenant defaults or property values fall.
findings.quote: At 31 March 2026 the Council held £3.983 million of a longstanding portfolio of 11 investment properties within the borough. These investments generated £257,000 of investment income for the Council in 2025/26 after taking account of direct costs, representing a rate of return of 6.45%

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee - Annual Treasury Management Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Strategic property investment fund showing unrealised loss: £2.8m market value against £3m book value
findings.detail: The CCLA Property Fund, a long-term strategic investment, is carried at £3m but had a market price of £2.8m at 31 March 2026. The fund has no defined maturity and the council notes that capital values will move up and down over months, quarters and years.
findings.matters: The £200k unrealised loss and exposure to property market volatility indicate potential for further balance sheet impacts if property valuations weaken further.
findings.figures: CCLA fund £3m book value, £2.8m market value (£200k loss)
findings.quote: The fair value for this fund is based on the market price which as at 31 March 2026 was £2.8 million

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee - Annual Treasury Management Report 2025-26
findings.headline: 82% of borrowing (£14m) matures within 12 months, creating high refinancing risk
findings.detail: The council's maturity structure shows that £14.02m of the £17.1m total borrowing is due within 12 months. This concentration of refinancing need exposes the council to significant interest rate risk, particularly given the volatile market conditions noted in the report.
findings.matters: High near-term refinancing need means the council must roll over debt annually; if rates remain elevated or rise further, refinancing costs will compound the already-significant overspend.

findings.paper_title: Audit Committee - Annual Treasury Management Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Financing costs overran budget by £995k (68%), raising the cost of borrowing from 5.64% to 6.36% of revenue
findings.detail: The council's financing costs outturn was £2.45m against a budget of £1.455m, an overspend of £995k. The ratio of financing costs to net revenue stream increased from 5.64% to 6.36%. This reflects higher-than-anticipated borrowing costs in a volatile interest rate environment.
findings.matters: Material cost overrun on debt service reduces financial headroom and suggests either debt volumes were higher than planned or interest rates proved significantly more expensive than modeled.
findings.figures: Financing costs £1,455k budgeted vs £2,450k actual (£995k overspend); ratio 5.64% estimated vs 6.36% actual
